narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video serves as a motivational advice piece targeting men in the dating market. The creator uses a provocative hook by claiming 'jerk men' are more successful because they are more 'hardworking' (investing time, money, and emotional effort). She then bridges this to a professional context, suggesting that in work, people fear those who are more privileged AND more hardworking. The ultimate intent is to challenge 'average' men to stop complaining about their lack of romantic success and instead increase their effort and proactive nature if they truly desire a relationship.
